buyer: NHS SOUTH WEST LONDON INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
title: Population Health Management (PHM)
description: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (SWL ICB) is carrying out preliminary market engagement ahead of a potential procurement of a Population Health Management (PHM), Population Segmentation and Risk Stratification platform, expected to be conducted through the G-Cloud 15 framework (RM1557.15), Lot 2b Software as a Service. For the avoidance of doubt, only suitable suppliers on G-Cloud 15 framework (RM1557.15), Lot 2b Software as a Service will be invited to submit a tender if the ICB decide to proceed with a call off with competition. This Request for Information (RFI) asks suppliers to describe their current capability against the full draft SWL PHM Service Specification. NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (SWL ICB) is seeking supplier information and indicative commercial proposals ahead of a planned procurement for a Population Health Management (PHM), Population Segmentation, Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling solution for its registered population of approximately 1.78 million residents across Croydon, Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton and Wandsworth. The requirement is intended to support the development of Integrated Neighbourhood Teams, proactive care, health inequalities reduction and population-based commissioning. The proposed solution should provide a clinically validated capability to segment the population, identify individuals at greatest risk of poor outcomes, determine which patients are most likely to benefit from proactive intervention, and support care coordination and neighbourhood delivery through actionable intelligence integrated into clinical workflows. The solution must support interoperability with existing SWL systems, including GP clinical systems and SWL Health Insights, and align with NHS clinical safety, information governance and interoperability standards. Suppliers on the G-Cloud 15 framework are invited to submit information on their current capability and provide indicative pricing proposals covering: 1. The full end-to-end service, including Population Health Management, Population Segmentation, Risk Stratification, Impactability Modelling, cohort identification, analytics, dashboards, integration, implementation, training and ongoing support. 2. A standalone Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling service, including clinically validated models for emergency admission risk, emergency department attendance risk, care coordination risk, frailty, end of life prediction and impactability modelling, together with the associated implementation, integration and support costs. This reflects SWL ICB's current business case focus on procuring a dedicated risk stratification and impactability capability while maintaining alignment with wider London population segmentation developments. Suppliers should clearly distinguish between costs for the full service and costs for the standalone Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling component, including one-off implementation costs and annual recurring charges. Responses will be used to inform business case development, affordability assessment, procurement strategy and market maturity analysis and will not constitute a formal tender evaluation

title: SPS-02377 Treatment of Recyclable and Residual Waste for SPS
description: The purpose of this Contract is to engage with a Supplier to ensure that the SPS operates in a safe, appropriate and environmentally compliant manner in relation to the management of Non-Hazardous Controlled Waste. Including the on-site storage, collection, transfer, treatment and subsequent disposal of all Non-Hazardous Controlled Waste across the SPS Estate. The Supplier shall ensure source segregation and separate collection of the following key materials, including but not limited to: Dry mixed Recyclables (Paper; Card; Glass; Metals; Cans; Plastics; Textiles; and Wood); and Residual Waste.

title: Asset Safety and Compliance (ASC2) - PME
description: Scottish Procurement Alliance (SPA) is developing its next-generation Asset Safety and Compliance Framework (ASC2), building upon the existing ASC1 framework. The potential scope of ASC2 is currently expected to include services relating to Asbestos consultancy, surveying and removal services, Property protection and security services, Water hygiene, testing and treatment services, Heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) compliance services, Electrical testing, inspection and remedial works, Building safety and associated compliance services and other statutory compliance disciplines identified through market engagement The above scope is indicative at this stage and may be amended or expanded following Preliminary Market Engagement and further development of the procurement strategy. Please refer to the attached ASC2 Preliminary Market Engagement document for further information on the proposed framework and details of how to register for the Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) event. Interested organisations are also encouraged to view the ASC2 opportunity on the LHC In-tend portal and express their interest in the opportunity to receive relevant updates and information: https://supplier.in-tend.co.uk/lhc/tenders/details/063e2d74-78cc-437f-9d27-4ae6b2fe0934

buyer: NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board
title: Integrated Urgent Care Services covering Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk and Central East (excl. Cambridge and Peterborough)
description:
NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board, NHS Essex Integrated Care Board and NHS Central East Integrated Care Board (together, the “Relevant Authorities”) are collaboratively considering the future commissioning of Integrated Urgent Care Services across their respective geographical footprints, excluding Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

The emerging scope includes NHS 111, Clinical Assessment Services, GP Out of Hours services and Urgent Care Coordination Hub arrangements. The ambition is to support more integrated and equitable access to urgent care, enabling patients to tell their story once, receive a trusted clinical assessment and be directed to the right care, closer to home where appropriate, while reducing avoidable pressure on emergency services.

The current planning assumption is that any future contractual arrangements would commence on 1 October 2028, following an indicative six-month mobilisation period, subject to governance approval, any future provider selection process and successful mobilisation.

This notice is being issued to support a programme of pre-procurement market engagement. The Relevant Authorities are seeking information and evidence from the market to inform future commissioning, service design and procurement decisions.

This is a planning notice for market engagement, not a call for competition, and does not invite tenders or commit the Relevant Authorities to a particular procurement route, service model, lotting structure or contract award. Final governance, delegation and contracting arrangements also remain to be agreed.
